> **Narrowed 2026-10-17 (backlog sweep).**
>
> **Resolved so far:** PR #1029 (`fix/labels-prices-contract`, `a141803a7`) -- item 3. `Feature()` now carries `labels_unmatched` through concatenation via a `feature._ATTRS_CARRIERS` entry, as `{country: report}`. This is a shape change for single-country readers: a one-kept-country `Feature` result used to carry the flat Country report (a one-frame concat keeps `attrs`). The multi-country fix is evidenced by synthetic tests (`tests/test_feature_attrs_carriers.py::TestLabelsUnmatchedSurvivesAssembly`); no measured real call has two kept countries with unmatched labels.
>
> **Remaining (this issue):**
> 1. Decide whether one Preferred Label mapping to multiple distinct nonmissing targets must raise instead of retaining last-row-wins (reviewed conflicts include Niger, Senegal, Burkina Faso and Uganda Cassava flour; do not choose a target by row order as a scientific ruling).
> 2. Curate each country's intended Aggregate/other label variants and missing mappings under the existing Aggregate contract.
> 3. Correct the numeric-target examples in `Guatemala/_/categorical_mapping.org` and `Serbia/_/categorical_mapping.org` when those countries next re-warm (hashed build inputs).
>
> (Old item 3, carrying `labels_unmatched` through `Feature`, is struck.) Unreconciled detail from #1029: `docs/guide/label-selection.md` quotes both 42,206 and 42,240 rows for the same Malawi `labels='2004-05'` call.

<details><summary>Previous issue text</summary>

Resolved so far: the reviewed development landings and source commits are recorded in [the v0.15.0 issue reconciliation](https://github.com/ligon/LSMS_Library/blob/8d7a5e55914e700c69ae1a195f96cc2282b6ce64/slurm_logs/release_landing_2026-10-14/RELEASE_ISSUES.org) (PR #998). This issue remains open for the scope below.

Implemented in the v0.15.0 candidate: label-column normalization, Preferred Label as a no-op, numeric-target refusal, unmatched-label warnings/attrs and LSMS_LABELS_STRICT. The earlier blank-target loss was already fixed by #925. These changes are covered by the reviewed label-selection tests.

Remaining:
1. Decide whether one Preferred Label mapping to multiple distinct nonmissing targets must raise instead of retaining last-row-wins. The reviewed conflicts include Niger, Senegal, Burkina Faso and Uganda Cassava flour; do not choose a target by row order as a scientific ruling.
2. Curate each country's intended Aggregate/other label variants and missing mappings under the existing Aggregate contract.
3. Carry labels_unmatched through Feature concatenation using the existing attrs carrier; warnings already survive.
4. Correct numeric-target examples in Guatemala/_/categorical_mapping.org and Serbia/_/categorical_mapping.org when those countries next rewarm. They are hashed build inputs and were deliberately not changed in this read-path increment.

Evidence: slurm_logs/release_landing_2026-10-14/ labels follow-up; docs/guide/label-selection.md; the aggregate-labels skill. Retain the issue until these residual semantics are resolved.

</details>

comments.body:
Two corrections to the body above, both mine, posted rather than edited in so the
record shows what changed.

**1. "18 of 22 food countries raise" is imprecise — and the imprecision cuts
against my own finding 1.** (Severity row 6, and the § 6 heading.)

It should read: **18 of 22 raise on the documented `labels='Aggregate'`; only 8
of 22 raise on *every* value.**

The 10 countries in bucket 2 of table A resolve a crosswalk and simply lack an
`Aggregate` column. They do **not** raise on their own variant — they return a
frame. That is exactly the point of finding 1: the 7 `Original`-only countries
(Benin, Burkina_Faso, CotedIvoire, Guinea-Bissau, Niger, Senegal, Togo) all
answer `labels='Original'` with a last-row-wins collapse, Tanzania answers
`labels='FTC'`, and Ethiopia and Mali answer their bare-fallback columns
(`2011-12`, `Code`, `FTC Code`, …) per finding 4. Stating it as a flat "18 raise"
makes the surface look more loudly-failing than it is, which understates the
silent findings.

Corrected counts, unambiguously:

| request | countries that raise (of 22 declaring `food_acquired`) |
|---|---:|
| `labels='Aggregate'` (the documented example) | **18** |
| *any* value — i.e. no crosswalk at all | **8** |
| some value is honoured | **14** |

**2. § 3, "the same branch a 'no table at all' country like GhanaLSS takes"** —
should be **"would take."** The `Feature` run I report used
`['Uganda','Malawi','Nigeria','Tanzania']`; GhanaLSS was dropped from the run
because it is 5.26M rows and its cache was being rebuilt concurrently. The
GhanaLSS claim is read off `country.py:2609-2615` and `feature.py:621-624`
(both `LabelUnavailableError`, one handler), not measured. Tanzania is the
measured case, and it exercises the identical branch.

Neither correction changes any measured number or the severity ranking.

— Sue

## Correction: a skill documents this contract, and part of what I filed is settled design

@ligon pointed out there is a skill for this. There is, and neither this issue's investigation nor I read it before filing:

**`.claude/skills/add-feature/food-acquired/aggregate-labels/SKILL.md`** (142 lines)

It changes the standing of several findings above. Recording that before anyone acts on them, because one of the proposed fixes would break behaviour the skill calls load-bearing.

### It independently corroborates finding A

> Only **4 of 16** food countries curate an Aggregate column.

Same four countries this issue measured — EthiopiaRHS, Malawi, Nigeria, Uganda — reached by a different route. The denominators differ (16 = countries with a food-label table; 22 = countries declaring `food_acquired`) but the numerator and the country list agree exactly. Two independent measurements agreeing is worth more than either alone.

It also explains this issue's late EthiopiaRHS correction:

> `labels='Aggregate'` matches **`'Aggregate Label'`** first, then bare **`'Aggregate'`** (both spellings are in use).

So the bare-column case is documented behaviour, not an accident.

### Finding E is NOT a defect — it is the settled contract

The `Feature()` drop-plus-warning I recorded above is deliberate, settled 2026-06 in PR #550, and named "Contract B, loud structured degrade":

| call | documented behaviour |
|---|---|
| `Country('Benin').food_acquired(labels='Aggregate')` | raises `LabelUnavailableError` (a `KeyError` subclass), listing available columns |
| `Feature('food_acquired')(labels='Aggregate')` | drops each country that cannot honour it, emits **one** aggregated warning, stamps `attrs['labels_unavailable']` |

The skill states the reasoning: it deliberately does *not* silently return only the curated countries (the pre-fix footgun, where omissions looked like build failures) and deliberately does *not* mix granularities. What this issue observed live — Tanzania dropped, warning raised, `attrs['labels_unavailable']` set — is the contract working, not failing.

### The skill also forbids one obvious "fix"

> **The raise-vs-degrade line in `_relabel_j` is load-bearing — keep it:** *missing curation* → `LabelUnavailableError` → degradable by Feature. *malformed table* → **plain `KeyError`**: a genuine defect, must surface loudly. *misuse* → **plain `KeyError`**. Do **not** convert the malformed-table or no-`j` cases to `LabelUnavailableError` to make a cross-country call "go green" — that would degrade over a real bug.

This bears directly on **finding C**. `labels='Preferred Label'` raising a bare `KeyError` rather than `LabelUnavailableError` is, by that taxonomy, the *correct* class — it is misuse, not missing curation, so it must stay loud and must **not** be made Feature-degradable. The defect in C is therefore narrower than I filed it: the exception **class is right**, the **message is bad** (a bare `KeyError: 'Preferred Label'` surfacing from a duplicate-column selection, telling the user nothing about which spellings are accepted). Fix the message; do not touch the class.

### What survives unchanged

Findings **1** (last-row-wins on a non-unique `Preferred Label` key: Niger 153 conflicting keys, Senegal 134, Burkina 72) and **2** (pass-through 0–67.1%; Ethiopia `labels='2011-12'` renames nothing for 51 of 76 `j` values carrying 46.6% of expenditure, with row count and total identical to the default read) are untouched by the skill — it documents the *contract*, not the rename mechanism, and neither behaviour is described anywhere in it. Those remain the substantive silent-wrong-answer findings, and they are the reason to act on this issue at all.

Finding **3**'s reframing (cross-country vocabulary mixing is pre-existing in the default read, not introduced by `labels=`) also stands.

### Process note

This is the fourth time in one session that machinery already existed and was rediscovered — after `units=`, `currency=` and `median_price_valuation`. The skill's own `description` field says precisely when to read it ("when calling `labels='Aggregate'` … and needing to know the API contract"), so the discovery path existed and went unused. `make api-audit` covers the *code* surface; it does not index `.claude/skills/`, which is a real gap in what was built for #783's sibling problem.

— Sue

## Re: the skill — agreed on two points, but the prohibition does not reach fix 6

I read `.claude/skills/add-feature/food-acquired/aggregate-labels/SKILL.md`
(142 lines) after the comment above. Confirming what it settles, and pushing
back on one thing, because as written the comment would leave a known-bad
proposal of mine standing while removing the fix for it.

### Agreed, and worth stating plainly

**Finding A is independently corroborated.** The skill says *"Only **4 of 16**
food countries curate an Aggregate column"* and names them (line 65):
EthiopiaRHS, Malawi, Nigeria, Uganda. That is exactly the set I measured, by a
different route and a different denominator (16 = countries with a food-label
table; my 22 = countries declaring `food_acquired`). Two independent
measurements agreeing is worth more than either.

**Contract B is settled design, and I did not file it as a defect.** Worth
being precise, since the comment above reads as though I did: § 3 of the issue
says of the drop-plus-warning *"That half is the **loud** half and it works"*
and *"Correct behaviour."* The skill (PR #550) confirms it. Nothing to change.
The `labels='Aggregate'` bare-column fallback is likewise documented at line 21,
so **finding 4 needs narrowing**: the fallback itself is documented for
`Aggregate`. What remains undocumented is that it also silently accepts `Code`,
`FDC ID`, `FTC Code`, `GD Category` and the per-wave columns (`2010Q3`,
`2011-12`, `1994a`, …). That narrower claim stands.

### Where I disagree: the prohibition names two cases, and this is neither

The comment says finding 5 (`labels='Preferred Label'`) is "misuse, must stay
loud", and that my fix 6 is forbidden. The skill's actual words (lines 57-59):

> Do **not** convert **the malformed-table or no-`j` cases** to
> `LabelUnavailableError` to make a cross-country call "go green"

Two cases, both named. `labels='Preferred Label'` is neither: the table is
well-formed (it *has* `'Preferred Label'` — that is the whole mechanism) and the
frame has a `j` level. The skill's "misuse" branch is specifically *"table has no
`j` level to relabel"* (line 55), which is not this. It is a fourth case the
taxonomy does not enumerate: **a bad argument value against a sound table.**

And the code already has a settled answer for that fourth case — it just applies
it inconsistently. Measured at `_relabel_j` with the real Uganda crosswalk and a
3-row synthetic frame (no microdata):

```python
C = ll.Country('Uganda'); t = C.categorical_mapping['harmonize_food']
# df: 3 rows, index (t, i, j), j = real Preferred Labels
C._relabel_j(df, <value>, reaggregate=False)
```

| `labels=` | class | Feature-degradable |
|---|---|---|
| `'Bogus'` | `LabelUnavailableError` | **True** |
| `'Aggregat'` (typo of `Aggregate`) | `LabelUnavailableError` | **True** |
| **`'Preferred Label'`** | **bare `KeyError: 'Preferred Label'`** | **False** |
| `'Code'` | *no error* — `j` becomes `[100, 101, 102]` | — |

The skill's first branch covers this: *"column absent → `LabelUnavailableError`
→ degradable."* A **typo** of the variant name degrades gracefully; the
**literal column name** dies with a bare `KeyError`. Same category of user
error, opposite classes — and the difference is an accident of resolution
order, not a taxonomy decision. `'Preferred Label'` resolves `target` to a
column that *is* present, so it slips past the absent-column check and dies
later inside `table[['Preferred Label','Preferred Label']]`.

So fix 6 is not forbidden. It is also not the fix I would land: **the first half
of fix 6 makes the question moot** — normalise the argument (strip a trailing
`' Label'`) before the `(None, 'Preferred')` no-op test, so `'Preferred Label'`
means `'Preferred'` and no error class is touched at all. That is the safe fix
and it is consistent with `'Aggregate Label'` already working. I withdraw only
the "failing that, raise `LabelUnavailableError`" clause as unnecessary, not as
prohibited.

The last row is its own small finding: `labels='Code'` silently succeeds and
changes the `j` index level from strings to integers. That is finding 4's
undocumented surface, demonstrated.

### Unchanged

Findings **1** (last-row-wins: Niger 153 conflicting keys, Senegal 134, Burkina
72) and **2** (pass-through 0–67.1 %; Ethiopia `labels='2011-12'` leaves 51 of
76 `j` values unrenamed carrying 46.6 % of expenditure, with row count, distinct
`j` and total identical to the default read) are untouched by the skill — it
documents the *contract*, not the rename mechanism. Finding **3**'s reframing
stands. Those remain the reason to act.

### On the process note

Fair, and I own it: I did not read the skill before filing, and the skill's
`description` names this exact situation. Concretely, it cost the issue one
wrong emphasis (finding 4 stated broader than true) and one unnecessary clause
in a proposed fix. It did **not** cost any measured number — and the skill's
independent 4-of-16 agreeing with my 4-of-22 is the useful check that came out
of the duplication.

— Sue

## A ninth finding, and it is the exact complement of #2: **blank-matched `j` collapses to the empty string, silently**

Surfaced while landing #783 (PR #789), which switches `labels=` on for six more countries. Not caused by that PR — measurable on `development` today. Filing here because it belongs to this report's surface, not to the consolidation.

**Mechanism.** `all_dfs_from_orgfile` builds cells with `s.strip()` and nulls nothing. A **blank** crosswalk cell therefore arrives as `''`, not `NaN`, survives `_relabel_j`'s `.dropna()` (`country.py:2634`), and lands in `rdict` as `Preferred Label -> ''`. Every item whose variant is blank is then renamed to the empty string and they all **collapse into a single `j=''`**.

Finding #2 says an unmatched `j` passes through unrenamed. This is the other half: a *matched-but-blank* `j` is renamed to nothing, and several dozen distinct foods merge into one row group. Both are silent; this one is arguably worse, because #2 at least leaves the label intact.

**Measured.** GhanaSPS `food_acquired(labels='FCT Label')`: **94 distinct `j` -> 20**, of which one is `''`, because 81 of that table's 98 rows have a blank `FCT Label`. 19 real labels + 1 `''` = 20. Confirmed directly — `j_head[0] == ''` on GhanaSPS `FCT Label`, GhanaLSS `2016-17`, and GhanaLSS `FCT Code`.

**Corpus-wide exposure** (config-only sweep over every country whose `Country.categorical_mapping` yields a `food_items`/`harmonize_food` table) — **17 columns across 4 countries**:

| country | columns with blank cells |
|---|---|
| GhanaLSS | all 7 per-round columns (37–147 blanks of 205) + `FCT Code` (24) |
| GhanaSPS | `2009-10` 13, `2013-14` 5, `2017-18` 7, `Food Codes` 3, **`FCT Label` 81 of 98** |
| Mali | `2014-15`, `2018-19`, `2021-22` — 2 each of 327 |
| Panama | `2003` — 1 of 81 |

**Pre-existing, and provably so**: **Mali already resolved `labels=` before #783** and carries the same blank cells, so `Country('Mali').food_acquired(labels='2014-15')` reproduces this with none of PR #789's changes.

**Numeric columns are immune.** `Country.categorical_mapping` parses with `to_numeric=True`, which turns a blank numeric cell into `NaN`, and `.dropna()` then removes it correctly — Guatemala's `FCT code` has 5 NaN and no `''`. So the bug is confined to **text** variant columns, which is most per-wave label columns.

**Severity.** This is a **silent wrong answer**, so by this report's own ranking it belongs alongside #1 and #2 rather than with the loud-and-correct raises.

**Suggested fix**, for whoever takes #2 (they share a call site and should probably be fixed together): treat a blank/whitespace-only target as *no mapping* rather than as a mapping to `''`, i.e. drop those pairs from `rdict` before the rename. Note that this **changes returned data for Mali today**, so it cannot ride along inside a change constrained to be data-invariant — which is exactly why PR #789 reports it here instead of fixing it.

Refs #783, #789.
